foundry.package_dir: models/rfd3/src/rfd3 -> site-packages/rfd3 (pyproject.toml:118-125; configs force-included as rfd3/configs, :127-130)
foundry.note: no tag at this commit (13 commits after v0.2.0); the commit is the pin. The version string comes from hatch-vcs at build time (pyproject.toml:105-108): a git checkout at the commit yields 0.2.1.dev13+g4010e3e2e; the archive has no .git and needs SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION=0.2.1.dev13+g4010e3e2e. The kit installs the rfd3 extra (.[rfd3]); the in-job pin list also carries the four cuequivariance 0.11.1 packages of the rf3 extra (pyproject.toml:60-64).

archive_recipe: git archive --format=tar --prefix=foundry-4010e3e2/ 4010e3e2e7350edada3e25a45c908c6bf407df4d <paths> | gzip -n -9  (foundry: pyproject.toml README.md LICENSE.md src models/rfd3/src models/rfd3/configs models/rf3/src models/rf3/configs models/rfd3na/src models/rfd3na/configs models/mpnn/src models/rfd3/docs/examples models/rfd3/docs/input_pdbs); build: SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION=0.2.1.dev13+g4010e3e2e pip install --no-deps <extracted dir>

pinned_stack.tested_on: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (sm90), driver 580.95.05, the versions below in two identical interpreters built by `recipe` (a documentation label; nothing reads or compares it)
pinned_stack.recipe: two Python 3.12.1 virtual environments with the same packages — <stock> (pristine: upstream at the pin, never touched by the kit's install.sh) and <kit> (the same, then opt/forward/xattempt_addon/install.sh applied once, STOCK.md 'Stack'): `pip install 'rc-foundry[rfd3]'` from the pinned commit or stock/foundry-4010e3e.tar.gz with environment/requirements.lock as constraints (torch 2.13.0+cu130, triton 3.7.1), the apex wheel below `--no-deps` into both, then `pip install -e ../common/opt_core -e opt` in both (README 'Setup')

apex.build: not distributed with the tree (no public wheel for this torch): built from the commit with APEX_CPP_EXT=1 APEX_CUDA_EXT=1 `python setup.py bdist_wheel` against torch 2.13.0+cu130 (nvcc 13.0.88, gcc 11.4.0, TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=8.0;9.0;10.0;12.0+PTX; 12 extension modules), then `pip install --no-deps <wheel>` into both interpreters; wheel_sha256 identifies the one wheel file the prebuilt container route accepts; a wheel compiled elsewhere has another digest
apex.engaged_by: upstream's own import guard, rfd3/model/layers/layer_utils.py:13-23: apex.normalization.fused_layer_norm.FusedRMSNorm bound as RMSNorm_ for every RMSNorm of the network when importable, torch.nn.RMSNorm otherwise; no flag, no kit lever
apex.census_word: KERNELS rmsnorm=engaged:apex.FusedRMSNorm(<n>-modules[+ext])@apex0.1 on every route of this stack, REQUIRED (routes.ROUTES: expected engaged; a pass bound to torch.nn.RMSNorm — fallback:torch.nn.RMSNorm(<n>-modules)@torch<version> — is refused, exit 5)
apex.installed_into: both interpreters (the pristine stock one and the kit-patched one)

optional_packages.name: apex
optional_packages.note: upstream's public install line (pip install 'rc-foundry[rfd3]') and pyproject carry no apex; its code binds apex's FusedRMSNorm when the module imports (layer_utils.py:13-23)

pinned_stack.in_job_pins_note: the full list of these stack versions, `pip freeze --all` of either interpreter (apex==0.1 is the stack's one addition to upstream's install line); environment/Dockerfile installs it and the recipe uses the lines as pip constraints
